title: Practice online
hook: talks, chanting and sittings now travel by screen

segments.voice: Yesterday: Rhys Davids, the Pali Text Society, and the people behind the page. Your line: the translators.

A laptop propped on a stack of books. On the screen, a grid of small windows: a woman by a candle, a man in a parked car, an older monk in a robe, someone whose cat keeps walking across the keyboard. A bell rings through tinny speakers, and every face in every window closes its eyes at once, in different rooms, in different time zones. Nobody says a word for a long while. Then the bell again, and a few people wave.
screen: `A GRID OF SMALL WINDOWS.` → `ONE BELL, MANY ROOMS.` → `EYES CLOSE AT ONCE.`

segments.voice: A dharma talk used to reach the people in the room. Now teachers record their talks, and students listen on a commute or while washing dishes, sometimes years later and continents away. A hall in Chicago held the speakers we met last week; a phone holds talks from the schools we've met on this road. Temples and monasteries stream their morning chanting and their services, so someone at a kitchen table can chant the refuges in Pali, or the Heart Sutra, along with a monastery they've never visited. Why does company matter? In the Pali texts, the Buddha's attendant Ananda once said that good friendship, good companions, must be half of the holy life. The Buddha corrected him. Not half: good friendship is the whole of the holy life. That's the Upaddha Sutta, in the Samyutta Nikaya. Online sitting is one way people try to keep that kind of company when a temple is far away, or when they're sick, caring for someone, or can't leave home. Teachers differ. Some welcome online sittings and teach on screen every week. Others say some things only happen in a shared room: the smell of incense, a teacher noticing your posture, a bow you can actually see. Some communities do both. The texts don't settle that question. What they do say is that company on the path matters.
screen: `TALKS THAT TRAVEL.` · `CHANTING CARRIED HOME.` · `GOOD FRIENDSHIP IS THE WHOLE.` · `TEACHERS DIFFER.` · then, large: `SITTING TOGETHER, APART.`

segments.voice: Practice the part that makes a group sitting work, starting and stopping together: when the bell rings, settle at once, without fidgeting into it, and let your breath go at its own pace. When it rings again, stop where you are, open your eyes, and give a small nod, the way people wave in the grid.
Practice online. Talks, chanting and sittings that travel by screen, so people far apart can keep company on the path.
Your line: sitting together, apart. Not half the path: the whole of it. See you tomorrow.
